title: Introduce fast-fail priority shim and customer escalation hotfix for hosted API error amplification
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: During a multi-tenant customer migration on 2026-02-28 we observed cascading 5xx/timeouts affecting several high-spend tenants. Root cause analysis indicates an interaction between aggressive client-side retries, per-proxy connection pool exhaustion, and a KV-cache compaction spike that amplified load and triggered transient model-serving OOM/latency spikes. This ticket implements a short-term hotfix (priority shim + fast-fail behavior) to stabilize customer-facing traffic during escalations, plus a rollout and follow-up work.
analysis:
Repro and signals: (1) Spike originates from orchestrated tenant migration with SDKs issuing parallel retry attempts for a subset of long-running requests; (2) Edge proxies open many concurrent backend connections for retries which starved local connection pools and caused request queueing inside serving proxies; (3) Compaction/eviction of KV cache was triggered when queued requests began invalidating large contexts, causing CPU/GC pressure in the runtime and some 5xx responses; (4) Observed correlation between tenant-scoped inflight counts and 5xx rate on serving nodes. Key metric links: dashboard: https://console.redwood/dashboards/hosted-api/tenant-escalation-2026, incident postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-02-28-customer-migration-escalation
Root cause hypothesis: Multiple layers retried concurrently without a shared tenancy-aware throttle. The runtime lacked a short-circuit fast-fail for requests that were highly likely to increase tail latency (non-idempotent long-running calls).
proposed_fix: 1) Edge hotfix: introduce a lightweight per-tenant priority shim at the edge proxy that enforces a small reservation token pool (default 8) and fast-fails excess requests with 429 + Retry-After. 2) Server-side: add transient-error classification to avoid automatic server-side retries when upstream signals capacity pressure (treat certain 5xx/timeouts as non-idempotent and fast-fail). 3) SDK guidance: add an opt-in idempotency flag and recommend exponential backoff with jitter for escalated tenants. 4) Instrument: new tenant-level inflight metric and alert. 5) Comms: immediate customer-facing notice and postmortem link.
tradeoffs: - Fast-failing reduces tail amplification but surfaces 429 to customers; we will provide transparent Retry-After and quick customer comms. - Token reservation reduces throughput headroom for noisy tenants; we tuned defaults conservatively to avoid impacting steady-state throughput. - This is an interim mitigation; it does not replace the longer-term per-tenant queuing and KV compaction guards.
hotfix_plan: A. Prepare proxy binary with shim (edge-proxy: v1.12-hotfix) and runtime guard (runtime: v2.3.1-hotfix). B. Canary rollout: deploy to region-us-east-1-edge-canary (5% traffic) for 30m. C. Monitor key metrics: tenant_inflight_count, proxy_conn_pool_usage, 5xx_rate_by_tenant, request_latency_p99. D. If stable, ramp to 25% for 1h, then to 100% in region. E. Cross-region rollouts follow same cadence. F. Rollback plan: if 5xx or customer reports increase, revert proxy to v1.11 within 15 minutes and scale back traffic.
tests_and_results: Unit tests: proxy shim tests for reservation and Retry-After header added. Integration: staged canary saw 62% reduction in tenant-induced backend queue depth and 45% reduction in p50->p99 amplification for the impacted tenant. Load tests: synthetic replay of migration traffic at 1.5x earlier peak showed runtime CPU pressure no longer triggers compaction OOMs in canary cluster. See CI run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/actions/runs/1423325 and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/runtime/pull/4839
canary_checklist:
- Deploy edge-proxy v1.12-hotfix to canary pool
- Validate headers: X-Redwood-Tenant-Inflight, Retry-After present
- Verify downstream logs show fast-fail rate for noisy tenant <= 5% of requests
- Confirm no increase in 5xx for non-noisy tenants
- Obtain signoff from oncall (Jonah Morales) and PM (Priya Nair)
